vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: team-dispatch
Version: 1.0.5

The bundle implements a complex multi-agent orchestration system that performs extensive system-level modifications and establishes persistence. Key indicators include `scripts/setup.sh`, which modifies the core `openclaw.json` configuration to grant broad `subagents.allowAgents` permissions, and `scripts/watch-install.sh`, which installs persistent background services via `launchd`, `systemd`, or `cron` to run a monitoring script (`scripts/watch.py`). While these high-risk behaviors are documented and aligned with the stated purpose of managing task dependencies (DAG), the combination of persistence and system-wide configuration changes represents a significant attack surface without clear evidence of malicious intent.

llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions match a multi-agent dispatcher, but its install/run instructions modify global OpenClaw agent configuration, install persistent watchers, and enable broad subagent permissions—actions that are coherent with the advertised purpose but carry notable security/scope risks and should be reviewed before running.

dimensions.detail: The skill's name/description (multi‑agent orchestration) aligns with the included assets: agent templates, DAG/project templates, watcher scripts, and setup scripts that create agent workspaces and dispatching behavior. However, the setup explicitly writes into global OpenClaw config (openclaw.json) and configures a 'main' dispatcher with subagents.allowAgents: ["*"], which is broader than a minimal skill install—plausibly intended but worth confirmation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs running scripts/setup.sh that will create symlinks, write ~/.openclaw/configs/team-dispatch.json, copy assets into ~/.openclaw/agents/<id>, create workspace/sessions, modify openclaw.json entries (adding main + subagents), and restart the Gateway. Those instructions require modifying system/global agent state and creating background jobs; they go beyond a purely local helper and grant the dispatcher broad control over agent configuration.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no external install spec (instruction-only), but the package includes many shell/Python scripts (setup.sh, watch.sh, watch.py, launchd plist, Windows scheduled task installer). Scripts are bundled (no obvious external download URLs in provided files), which reduces supply-chain unknowns, but executing them will write files, create scheduled tasks/launchd plists, and restart services—operations that deserve manual review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential. Optional notification features (Telegram chatId) and model names are present in configs but disabled by default. Requesting no external secrets is proportionate to the stated purpose; still, if you enable notifications or model access, you will need to provide credentials externally.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The setup writes persistent files across ~/.openclaw (configs, agents, workspaces), installs a periodic watcher (cron/launchd/scheduled task), and modifies openclaw.json and Gateway state. It also configures main.subagents.allowAgents: ["*"], which grants broad subagent allowance. These are persistent, privileged changes that affect other agents and the system-wide agent registry—appropriate for a dispatcher but a clear escalation in system presence and blast radius.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill generally does what it says (set up a dispatcher and subagents), but be cautious before running its setup scripts. What to do before installing:
- Inspect scripts/setup.sh, scripts/watch.sh, watch.py and any files that write to ~/.openclaw or openclaw.json; don't run blindly. Look for commands that download or execute remote code.
- Backup ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and any existing ~/.openclaw/agents before running setup, so you can restore prior configuration.
- The setup will restart the Gateway and install a background watcher (launchd/cron/scheduled task). If you don't want persistent background jobs, disable that step or remove the watcher assets before installing.
- The config sets main.subagents.allowAgents: ["*"]. Consider restricting this to a specific list of agent IDs instead of "*" to avoid allowing arbitrary agents broad privileges.
- Notification hooks (Telegram) are disabled by default; only enable and provide chat IDs/keys if you trust the code and understand where messages will be sent.
- Prefer to run the install steps manually (as an informed user) rather than letting an agent run them autonomously—this gives you a chance to review and control each change.
If you want, I can summarize or walk through specific scripts line-by-line and flag exact commands that create/modify files, restart services, or perform network activity.
